theories.claim: QAStore.VerificationBytes fails to reject symlinked directories inside verification because it tests entry.Info().Mode()&os.ModeSymlink after filepath.WalkDir, which follows symlinks for Info and loses the ModeSymlink bit
theories.basis: Read internal/sprint/qa_state.go:46-78. VerificationBytes resolves root via store.resolve (which Lstats each component) then calls filepath.WalkDir and inside walkFn does info,err:=entry.Info(); if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink!=0 return error. Elsewhere in repo the correct pattern is os.Lstat (e.g., verify.go:405 targetIdentity uses os.Lstat(full) to detect symlink, qa_state.go:199 resolve uses os.Lstat(current)). Go's DirEntry.Info for a symlink-to-directory Stats the target (regular dir, IsDir true, ModeSymlink cleared) while DirEntry.Type preserves ModeSymlink. WalkDir does not descend into symlinked dirs (IsDir false), so the symlink is treated as leaf, not error, not counted, silently ignored.
theories.verification_surface: internal/sprint/qa_state.go:46-78 VerificationBytes WalkDir callback; contrast internal/sprint/qa_state.go:183-210 resolve Lstat loop and internal/sprint/verify.go:349-443 targetIdentity Lstat+EvalSymlinks+inside check
theories.confirmation_condition: Static code shows VerificationBytes uses entry.Info() rather than entry.Type() or os.Lstat(path) to test symlink, and Go DirEntry.Info follows the symlink for directory targets, so a symlink directory entry will have ModeSymlink==0 and not trigger the error
theories.refutation_condition: Demonstrate via Go stdlib documentation or local Go source that filepath.WalkDir DirEntry.Info for a symlinked directory on this Go version preserves ModeSymlink, or that WalkDir follows symlinked directories and still surfaces ModeSymlink
theories.inconclusive_condition: Cannot inspect runtime Go stdlib DirEntry implementation or execute filesystem symlink test on this host to observe Info vs Type behavior
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read-only: inspect qa_state.go, verify.go, artifacts.go inside() helper, workspace.ResolveInside, and PruneAttempts similar pattern; compare Info vs Lstat usage; review Go filepath.WalkDir documentation without creating files or executing commands; no mutation, no shell

theories.outcome_reason: Code inspection confirms vulnerable pattern: VerificationBytes is the only verification-area size scan that relies on entry.Info() ModeSymlink, mismatched with the Lstat-based checks used in resolve() and targetIdentity(). Combined with WalkDir not descending into symlink dirs, this predictably allows a symlinked subdirectory (e.g., verification/attempts -> /tmp/evil) to be ignored rather than rejected, bypassing the intended symlink rejection and the StateBytes budget accounting. Root-level symlink verification dir is correctly rejected by resolve() Lstat loop, so escape is interior but still violates contract-security symlink rejection.

theories.claim: VerificationBytes directory-symlink miss allows StateBytes budget bypass: large external content behind an interior symlink is not counted, so RetainedAttempts budget enforcement via VerificationBytes() in RunQA can be evaded
theories.basis: Read internal/sprint/qa.go:272-276 check if used,err:=store.VerificationBytes(); used>StateBytes then BudgetExhausted. If VerificationBytes silently skips symlinked subdirectories due to theory 1, an attacker with write access to verification could place external large store via symlink and not be counted, evading persistence budget and potentially hiding malicious state.

theories.claim: QAStore.PruneAttempts uses entry.Info().Mode()&ModeSymlink on ReadDir entries, which may also follow symlink-to-directory targets and could miss the symlink bit, relying instead on !entry.IsDir gate
theories.basis: Read internal/sprint/qa_state.go:82-136. PruneAttempts lists attempts via os.ReadDir, first checks if !entry.IsDir()||!validQAIDKind, then does info,err:=entry.Info(); if ModeSymlink. For a symlink to a directory, ReadDir DirEntry.IsDir is false (Type includes ModeSymlink) so the first gate already triggers InvalidState but with generic invalid-entry message, not the explicit unsafe-entry symlink message, and the subsequent Info-based symlink test may be ineffective due to Stat-following behavior. Inconsistent with Lstat usage elsewhere.
theories.confirmation_condition: Show that PruneAttempts symlink-directory case depends on Info rather than Type/Lstat and therefore does not reliably report unsafe symlink, or that removal logic could operate on wrong target
theories.refutation_condition: Show that ReadDir DirEntry.Info on this platform preserves ModeSymlink or that !entry.IsDir gate is sufficient to reliably reject all symlink attacks with appropriate error category
theories.inconclusive_condition: Cannot execute filesystem symlink test to observe ReadDir Info vs Type behavior without shell execution
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read-only comparison of PruneAttempts vs resolve vs targetIdentity symlink handling; inspect Go os.DirEntry documentation for ReadDir Type vs Info semantics; no file creation or execution
